eventmodeling.comment: Read the eventmodeling header and its required following boundary. eventmodeling.md#header-boundary: Only the eventmodeling keyword has an additional boundary: the next characters must be %%, common Notation whitespace, or end of text. This includes LS, PS, NBSP and BOM, but excludes U+0085 and U+200B. A glued percent comment can follow it; a glued slash comment cannot. A space before the slash comment supplies the boundary. Judge this after common removals: a removed directive leaving space or LF succeeds, while eventmodeling joined to tf, or tf joined to digits, rejects.

patterns.comment: Read native hidden YAML. eventmodeling.md#native-hidden-forms-and-comments: In [the hidden rules][hidden], hidden-yaml starts with three dashes, optional ASCII space/tab and LF. It has an unindented three-dash closer followed by LF, another Notation whitespace character or end of text. Try a body of at least one line before the adjacent empty form, with the same closing choice as block-data. Four opening dashes or an indented closer fail. It does not parse YAML or apply configuration. A following LF is consumed, other boundary whitespace is not.

Read native hidden directives. eventmodeling.md#native-hidden-forms-and-comments: Hidden-directive reads optional ASCII space/tab, %%{, any characters including LF/LS/PS, then the first }%% whose following boundary is LF, other Notation whitespace or end of text. A following LF is consumed; other whitespace is only looked ahead at. A nonqualifying earlier closer can be included while seeking a later qualifying closer. Separate this from global directive removal: word-named forms such as %%{x}%% may already have disappeared. Nonword forms establish the native behavior.

Read native percent comments, retaining comment-looking text. eventmodeling.md#native-hidden-forms-and-comments: If hidden-directive fails, try percent-comment: %% through before CR/LF or end of text, including a bare %%. Comment lines are read by this rule too, since they are not removed before the lexer reads the text; inside a block value, a slash block comment or a hidden form, a comment line is part of that text. A comment line ends only at CR or LF: a U+2028 or U+2029 in it does not end it, so `%% a`, a U+2028, and `tf 01 evt A` is all one comment. A global directive in a comment line is removed, as everywhere, and the rest of the line stays in the comment: in `%% a %%{init: {}}%% tf 09 evt Z` the frame is part of the comment, and inside a data block the line `%% c %%{init: {}}%% d` leaves `%% c`, two spaces, and `d` in the value.

Read slash comments; whole directives preserve their own scopes. eventmodeling.md#native-hidden-forms-and-comments: Slash-block-comment reads `/*` through the first `*/`, without nesting and requiring closure; its body may contain LF, LS and PS. Slash-line-comment reads `//` through before CR/LF or end of text; LS and PS do not end it. Their marks are `/*` and `//`, their values exclude the marks and the block closer, and outside padding is not content. Comments can occupy complete-unit gaps but do not join identifier fragments. Global directives can lie inside comment text or between the mark characters; a comment line inside a slash block comment is part of its text. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.

patterns.comment: Read the diagram-specific padded metadata forms. eventmodeling.md#common-statements: Title-line reads optional ASCII space/tab padding, title, then either one ASCII space/tab and any non-CR/LF line text, or an empty suffix. Accessibility-title-line reads that padding, accTitle, optional ASCII space/tab, colon and line text. Description-line uses accDescr in the same form and takes precedence over its brace alternative. Line text may be empty and includes LS/PS; prefer ending it immediately before the first %%, otherwise take it through the end of the line. Bare title is permitted, but unreadable text after its bare-prefix match still rejects. No later line supplies a missing line value. eventmodeling.md#common-statements: Description-block reads padded accDescr, any Notation whitespace, an opening brace, any characters through the first closing brace, and that closer. It may span LF, LS and PS. Quotes and backslashes do not shield a closer, and unclosed forms reject. Empty blocks remain statements. Do not trim the authored interior: whitespace-only content remains a literal. Global removals can make payloads empty without removing the authored statement or data shell.

Read statement and clause keywords, leaving longer identifiers whole. eventmodeling.md#ordered-units: Every word keyword has identifier as its explicit longer alternative: a strictly longer identifier wins, but an equal-length keyword wins. Punctuation has no longer alternative. Matching is case-sensitive. This is not Jison word-boundary matching: tf01 and evtA are identifiers, while a numeric frame-name can touch the next type keyword. Exact ordinary keywords cannot be identifiers, but longer words such as eventX can.

Read entity-type words, leaving longer identifiers whole. eventmodeling.md#ordered-units: Every word keyword has identifier as its explicit longer alternative: a strictly longer identifier wins, but an equal-length keyword wins. Punctuation has no longer alternative. Matching is case-sensitive. This is not Jison word-boundary matching: tf01 and evtA are identifiers, while a numeric frame-name can touch the next type keyword. Exact ordinary keywords cannot be identifiers, but longer words such as eventX can. eventmodeling.md#preserving-occurrences: Preserve the entity-type word of each GWT item even though the upstream unassigned grammar call omits it from its model.

Read separate type-tag delimiters and the data type. eventmodeling.md#data: The [data fragments][data] permit an optional tag: opening backtick, one of json, jsobj, figma, salt, uri, md, html or text, then closing backtick. These are separate components with native gaps between them; the following body is required. Empty or unknown tags reject. The tag does not validate its body as JSON, a URI or another language. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.

Read source arrows, data-reference brackets and qualified-name dots. eventmodeling.md#authored-component-boundaries: For the shared directive and selected-semicolon rules, each header/statement/common keyword, entity/data-type word, identifier segment, frame-name digit string, complete ->>, [[ and ]] is an atom. A directive or selected semicolon inside one of these rejects here. Qualified-name dot punctuation, type-tag backticks and type word, reference opener/name/closer, arrow/reference name and common keyword/colon/brace/value are separate authored components. Global removal between them is allowed only when the remaining lexical boundaries still match. Native hidden forms do not gain the power to split an atom.
Read a frame name, retaining leading zeros. eventmodeling.md#names-and-references: A frame-name is a string of one to three ASCII digits, not a quantity: 1, 01 and 001 are distinct names.
patterns.name: variable.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read inline brace or quoted data through the last same-line closer; retain whole directives. eventmodeling.md#data: The [inline-data rule][data-terminals] tries braces, double quotes, then single quotes. It reads through the last matching closer on the same line, including earlier closers and apparent later statements. CR, LF, LS and PS cannot be inside it. Backslash is ordinary content and protects neither quote nor brace. Empty braces and empty quoted strings are accepted. Inline data has priority over block data at the same position, even where the grammar requires a block. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text. common.md#html-attribute-quotes: The lexer reads the two `"` of each quoted value as `'`.

Read block-data brace delimiters and text, retaining comment-looking body content. eventmodeling.md#data: Block-data starts with an opening brace, zero or more ASCII spaces/tabs and LF. Its closer is an unindented brace immediately after LF, followed by LF, another Notation whitespace character or end of text. Opening NBSP or LS, an indented closer and a closer immediately after LS reject. The interior can contain every character, including LS and PS. Missing closure rejects. eventmodeling.md#native-hidden-forms-and-comments: Comment lines are read by this rule too, since they are not removed before the lexer reads the text; inside a block value, a slash block comment or a hidden form, a comment line is part of that text. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.

Read an identifier segment or data-reference name. eventmodeling.md#names-and-references: The [name rules][names] read an identifier as an ASCII letter or underscore followed by zero or more ASCII letters, digits or underscores.

eventmodeling-statements.comment: Collect the padded title and accessibility forms. eventmodeling.md#common-statements: These composite forms precede native whitespace but follow identifier. They can claim a leading ASCII space/tab run at the current position. Judge LF and padding after common removals: global directives and the semicolons selected by the common line rule. A comment line is not removed: it is a native percent-comment, which ends before its LF, so the LF stays and native whitespace takes the indentation of the next line, and a comment line followed by an indented title, accTitle or accDescr is rejected. Removing a closed global directive alone leaves the LF outside it; removing a selected semicolon leaves any LF as well. A blank line also leaves LF. Whether a form can claim indentation on the next line then depends on whether the preceding unit consumed the remaining LF. If it did, the indentation begins at the current position and can enable the composite before native whitespace. If it did not, native whitespace starts at LF and consumes the indentation, leaving identifier to win at the keyword. Block-data, hidden-yaml and hidden-directive consume their closing LF; without indentation, identifier still wins on the following line. Common CRLF conversion leaves the same LF case. LS and PS after these closers are not consumed: native whitespace starts there and takes the padding before a common form. On the same physical line, a surviving ASCII space/tab run can enable the composite, including across an inline global directive or a selected semicolon. An unselected semicolon is not whitespace and rejects in that gap. An empty description block remains a statement; it leaves its following LF unconsumed, but a common form can claim padding directly after its closing brace on the same line. In a name position, padded title can steal the position as a composite, whereas unpadded title can be an identifier. accTitle and accDescr without their required delimiters are identifiers.
